topic: Signal starts blocking screenshots so phone AI assistants like Siri and Gemini can't read your chats
announced_at: 20 November 2026 (Signal blog post by Meredith Whittaker; coverage 20-21 Nov)
window_expansion_reason: No strong verified story inside the 24 hours (21-22 Nov): the search index held only newsletter digests for 21 Nov, whose items were either older (chip approvals and the Dragos study, 19 Nov; ChatGPT Wallet, 13 Nov), extraordinary and unverified (a claimed Riemann Hypothesis proof), or financial claims needing an unopenable primary (Nvidia SEC report). Widened to 48 hours, which brings in Signal's 20 Nov announcement.
why_selected: Strongest verified story in the widened 48-hour window: Signal's own announcement (indexed text) plus six independent outlets, about a privacy fight that touches every phone user.
why_short: A messaging app is blocking the AI on your own phone: relatable, surprising, and easy to discuss.
why_beats_alternatives: The House chip-approval disclosure and the Dragos prompt-canary study were released on 19 Nov (before even the widened 48-hour window) and rely on secondary figures; the Claude Riemann Hypothesis proof claim is extraordinary, single-sourced and conflicts with the writer's disclosure; ChatGPT Wallet (13 Nov) and Walmart's Agent Gateway (21 Oct) are outside the window.
verified_development: On 20 Nov 2026 Signal announced screenshot blocking on iOS 27 (default 'Block Siri AI' setting) and detection-based Screen security on some Android versions, to keep OS-level AI assistants out of chats (Signal blog indexed text plus 9to5Mac, Android Authority, Decrypt, Digital Trends, gHacks, CyberInsider).
disclosure: Disclosure: this package was written by Claude, an Anthropic model. The story concerns Apple, Google and Signal; Anthropic is not involved.
research_summary: Signal president Meredith Whittaker's blog post 'Signal is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy' (20 Nov 2026) says AI agents built into operating systems, such as Apple's Siri AI and Google's Gemini, are an existential threat to private messaging. Signal now blocks in-app screenshots by default on iOS 27 through a 'Block Siri AI' setting, and turns on Screen security on Android versions where it can detect an assistant reading the screen. macOS cannot be reliably protected; Signal recommends excluding Signal from Siri there. Users can switch the protection off, with a warning that it exposes their and their contacts' messages. Signal admits agents could still read data stored on the device and asks Apple, Google and Microsoft for an official opt-out. It follows Signal's 2025 move against Windows Recall.

script:
Signal just started blocking screenshots. And the reason is AI.

Signal says the AI assistants built into your phone, like Siri and Gemini, can read what's on your screen. Including your private chats.

So on iPhones running iOS 27, screenshots inside Signal are now blocked by default. On some Android phones, Signal switches on a screen shield when it spots an AI assistant reading.

You can turn it off. But Signal warns that exposes your contacts' messages too.

Its president calls this kind of AI an existential threat. And Signal admits the fix isn't complete.

So, would you trade AI convenience for privacy?
